reason: The cited evidence supports the general effectiveness of laser cladding for wear resistance and metallurgical bonding on H13 steel, but it does not mention Ti(C,N)-based ceramic reinforcements, their in situ synthesis, or their uniform dispersion, leaving the core material-specific premises unsupported.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a metallurgically bonded layer with low dilution and rapid cooling.
Laser cladding is an effective method for enhancing surface wear resistance of steel.
In situ synthesized Ti(C,N)-based ceramic reinforcements can be formed and uniformly dispersed via laser cladding.
Uniformly dispersed hard ceramic phases increase surface hardness and wear resistance.
